title: yadgar/task
$comment: ADR-0847 (closed schemas; render checks own types) and ADR-0850 (closure is per chart — this file closes only the keys `task` itself owns). Untyped closure at every block, typed nowhere: a mapping becomes `properties` + `additionalProperties: false` with no `type`, so a scalar or null written where a block belongs passes THIS schema and reaches render-checks.yaml instead (ADR-0794/0797, landed by D-M ledger 1135, task#71) — `autoscaling: "x"` is that file's territory, not this one's. A leaf is `{}`: no type, no enum, no default, no required. The two exceptions, both landed by C-SVb (ADR-0845): `tls.enabled` and `taskDb.tls.enabled` NOW carry `type: boolean` and their parent blocks carry `required: [enabled]` — the binary has no compiled-in default for either `LISTEN_TLS_ENABLED` or `TASK_DB_TLS_ENABLED` any more, so this chart can have none for the values that render them either. `chart/ci/values.yaml` ships both `true` so every shared gate that lints or renders this chart offline still has a value to coalesce (C-A2). B-U5 (ADR-0854) adds `clientAuth` to `tls`'s `required` and NOTHING else: the leaf stays `{}`, because `templates/render-checks.yaml` owns its type and its three values (`off`, `optional`, `required`) — a schema `type` or `enum` would pre-empt the named refusal a bare `off` needs (YAML reads it as false). `chart/ci/values.yaml` ships it `"off"`. Open maps, and why: `global` (every module in the parent's coalesced tree receives it whether or not this chart's own templates read `.Values.global`, ADR-0850 — an undeclared `global` refuses the parent's own default render); `resources` (templates/deployment.yaml does `toYaml .Values.resources` unexamined); `rollingUpdate` (`{{- with .Values.rollingUpdate }}` writes back whatever map it is handed, so `rollingUpdate: {}` returning the field to Kubernetes' own default has to stay legal). `networkPolicy.clients` is a list, not a block, and lists are `{}` too: its items are unindexed strings (`range $clients`), not gateway's typed peer objects — this chart's copy of networkpolicy.yaml is not gateway's. The keys `values.yaml` omits by design (extras, measured by grepping `chart/templates` for `.Values` paths `values.yaml` does not declare): `image.digest` (templates/deployment.yaml reads it to build the published image reference; ci-release rewrites it at package time, D65); `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` (values.yaml ships `scrapeFrom: {}`; templates/networkpolicy.yaml reads the nested key directly); and `tls.clientCaSecret`, `tls.clientCaSecretKey` — declared by the B-U5E expand (ADR-0854): `templates/deployment.yaml` mounts the client CA only when `tls.enabled` is true and `clientCaSecret` names a Secret, and `values.yaml` ships neither. All four are declared as leaves inside otherwise-closed blocks, so `scrapeFrom` is a closed one-key block rather than staying the open map its empty default would otherwise draft.
